reason: E2 supports the existence of Ta/Zr segregation and dual BCC phases in the as-cast alloy, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for local thermal expansion mismatch, the generation of internal residual stresses, or their influence on dislocation dynamics and elastic moduli. The cited evidence only loosely supports the first premise, leaving the core mechanistic premises unsupported.
premises: As-cast HfNbTaTiZr contains microstructural heterogeneities (e.g., dual BCC phases, nanoscale precipitates) due to segregation of Ta and Zr.
These heterogeneities cause local differences in thermal expansion coefficients.
Thermal expansion mismatch generates internal residual stresses upon heating/cooling.
These internal stresses alter dislocation dynamics and effective elastic moduli.
The mechanism unifies observations from creep, cold rolling, elastic measurements, and aging hardening.
